titular: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia and the shares fall as much as 14%
resum: Nvidia's founder has stepped down as chief executive with immediate effect, and chief financial officer Colette Kress is taking over on an interim basis. The shares fell as much as 14% (−14%) shortly after Thursday's open and closed down 4.34% at $166.19, while AMD and Broadcom rose more than 5%.
per_que_importa: Nvidia makes the chips that almost all AI runs on and is one of the world's most valuable companies, so a change at the top rattles stock markets and pension funds. The exit, linked by press reports to a personal controversy, opens a period of uncertainty just when the sector was already jittery.

titular: Anthropic's IPO draws six times more demand than shares on offer
resum: New: investors have asked for about 6 times the shares Anthropic is selling, according to Bloomberg, and the banks are considering pricing them above the planned $70–78 range. According to the Financial Times, the valuation could rise from $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion; the price would be set on 18 November, with the Nasdaq debut on the 19th.
per_que_importa: It would be the biggest IPO in history and a test of how much confidence there is in the AI business. But a full order book doesn't guarantee the shares will rise afterwards: several analysts point to cases with strong early demand that ended badly.

titular: OpenAI raises $15bn, half of what it was after
resum: The maker of ChatGPT has raised $15bn at a valuation of $1.25 trillion, according to CNBC. It was initially seeking up to $30bn at $1.4 trillion; even so, the valuation is 47% higher than in March ($852bn).
per_que_importa: It shows investors are still putting money into AI, but more cautiously and at a lower price than OpenAI wanted. The company brings in a lot (about $10bn in the third quarter), but still loses more than it earns because of the huge cost of data centres.

titular: SoftBank and Nvidia bet $500m on Agile Robots' German humanoid robots
resum: Munich-based Agile Robots has raised $500m in a round led by SoftBank, with Nvidia and Hitachi, valuing it at $8.5bn. That is less than the $800m talked about in June, and the company hasn't said how many humanoids it has actually delivered.
per_que_importa: It is one of the few big European bets on humanoid robots, a market dominated by US and Chinese companies. The money will go towards building more in Germany and expanding in the US, which could bring skilled industrial jobs to Europe.

titular: Amazon releases a free program written entirely by AI agents
resum: Amazon Web Services has launched AWS Emulator, a free tool that mimics more than 200 of its cloud services so developers can run tests on their own computers. According to the company, the code was written by AI agents without any engineer reviewing it line by line, although it doesn't replicate some security controls.
per_que_importa: It is a clear example of how programming work is changing: engineers are moving from writing code to designing tests and keeping an eye on what the machines do. For businesses it could make development cheaper, but it also raises questions about quality and accountability if something goes wrong.
xifra_text: Amazon services the tool mimics locally

titular: Google launches an AI that only answers yes, no or picks from options
resum: Gemini Decision 1 doesn't write text: it scores closed answers (yes/no, multiple choice or a rating) and can handle up to 1,000 questions at once about the same document, image or video. It costs $0.10 per million input 'tokens' (chunks of text) and is aimed at developers.
per_que_importa: Many companies use AI to sort emails, review documents or filter content, and a specialised model can do it far more cheaply and quickly. Making these tasks cheaper speeds up the automation of repetitive admin work.

titular: J.P. Morgan expects up to 400,000 humanoid robots to be built in the US in 2030
resum: The bank estimates US humanoid production will reach 300,000–400,000 units in 2030 and about 1.5 million in 2035, driven by labour shortages in factories and warehouses. It warns, however, that the robots' hands, motors and 'brains' are still holding growth back.
per_que_importa: If the forecast comes true, humanoids will start covering night shifts and hard-to-fill jobs, which could ease staff shortages but also put pressure on wages in low-skilled work. It is a bank's forecast, not actual data.

titular: Runway gives away Praxis-1, a robot 'brain' anyone can use
resum: Runway, known for its AI-generated videos, has released Praxis-1, a model that controls robots based on what it has learned from videos, with open weights and a licence that allows commercial use. The company says it succeeds at 46.2% of the tasks in an Nvidia benchmark, a figure not yet verified independently.
per_que_importa: Until now, training robots required huge numbers of expensive demonstrations; learning from videos could make it much cheaper. Being free means start-ups and universities, in Europe too, can try out robots without relying on a big tech company.

titular: UK-based Fractile raises $720m to make AI chips without having sold a single one
resum: Chip start-up Fractile has raised $720m at a valuation of about $7bn, according to Reuters and the Financial Times, seven times more than in May. Its first commercial chip won't arrive until 2027.
per_que_importa: It shows investors' appetite for alternatives to Nvidia in the chips that power AI. But it is a risky bet: a lot of money is being paid for technology that has not yet proved itself on the market.

titular: Juan Roig's fund invests in Ploot, a Valencian AI to help sell more
resum: Ploot, a Valencia start-up that uses AI to help companies' sales teams, has closed a €400,000 round led by Angels Capital, the investment firm of Juan Roig (owner of Spanish supermarket chain Mercadona). It has more than 3,000 users and wants to build its own sales agent.
per_que_importa: It shows that AI applied to specific tasks, such as winning customers, is also attracting investors in Spain. For small and medium-sized businesses, these tools can make sales work more efficient without big teams.
